- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, suppress the next 3–5 days’ forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction by 2–5% per day.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is erratic, smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days drop), adjust forecast to reflect downward momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
